questp1-basics#1.en: A fair ${N}-sided die is rolled once. How many outcomes are in the sample space, n(S)?

questp1-basics#2.en: The sample space is every value the die could land on.

questp1-basics#5.en: A fair ${N}-sided die is rolled. How many outcomes give ${e.desc}? (that is n(E))

questp1-basics#6.en: List the values that fit, then count them.

questp1-basics#9.en: A fair ${N}-sided die is rolled. Write P(${e.desc}) as a fraction in simplest form.

questp1-basics#13.en: A fair ${N}-sided die is rolled. Write P(${e.desc}) as a decimal (2 places).

questp1-basics#14.en: Work out n(E) / n(S), then divide it out.

questp1-basics#16.en: A fair ${N}-sided die is rolled. Write P(${e.desc}) as a percentage${pdp ? " (1 decimal place)" : ""}.

questp1-basics#17.en: Find P as a decimal, then × 100 for a percentage.

questp1-basics#24.en: An experiment is run ${total} times and "${thing}" happens ${hits} times. What is the relative frequency of "${thing}"? (decimal, 2 places)

questp1-basics#25.en: relative frequency = times it happened ÷ total trials.

questp1-basics#27.en: Which one is worked out before doing any experiment — just from the possible outcomes?

questp1-basics#32.en: One is a prediction; the other is what actually happened.

questp1-basics#33.en: Theoretical probability is the prediction; relative frequency comes from real data.

questp1-basics#35.en: A probability must lie between 0 and 1. Which of these cannot be a probability?

questp1-basics#36.en: 0 = impossible, 1 = certain. Nothing can be more likely than certain.

questp1-basics#37.en: ${bad} is outside the 0–1 range, so it is impossible as a probability.

questp2-venn-regions#3.en: On a Venn diagram, the symbol ∩ (the overlap of the circles) is read as…

questp2-venn-regions#8.en: It's the region that is in BOTH circles at once.

questp2-venn-regions#9.en: ∩ means “and” — the outcomes in A and B at the same time.

questp2-venn-regions#10.en: The symbol ∪ (everything in either circle) is read as…

questp2-venn-regions#14.en: It's everything in A together with everything in B.

questp2-venn-regions#15.en: ∪ means “or” — everything in A or B (or both).

questp2-venn-regions#17.en: everything that is not in A

questp2-venn-regions#18.en: everything in both A and B

questp2-venn-regions#20.en: the overlap of A and B

questp2-venn-regions#22.en: A′ = not A = everything outside circle A.

questp2-venn-regions#23.en: Tap the region that represents A ∩ B (A and B).

questp2-venn-regions#24.en: “A and B” is where the two circles overlap.

questp2-venn-regions#25.en: Look for the lens-shaped overlap in the middle.

questp2-venn-regions#26.en: A ∩ B is the overlap of the two circles.

questp2-venn-regions#27.en: Tap the region that is in ${which[1]} but not ${which[2]}.

questp2-venn-regions#28.en: That is the part of circle ${which[1]} that does NOT overlap ${which[2]}.

questp2-venn-regions#29.en: Avoid the overlap — you want one circle only.

questp2-venn-regions#30.en: “Only ${which[1]}” is the part of ${which[1]} outside the overlap.

questp2-venn-regions#31.en: Tap the region for (A ∪ B)′ — outcomes in neither A nor B.

questp2-venn-regions#32.en: Inside the rectangle, but outside both circles.

questp2-venn-regions#33.en: “Neither” lives in the rectangle, outside every circle.

questp2-venn-regions#34.en: Neither A nor B = inside S but outside both circles.

questp2-venn-regions#42.en: Which set does the shaded region represent?

questp2-venn-regions#43.en: Name exactly the part that is filled in.

questp2-venn-regions#45.en: For any event A and its complement A′, what is P(A) + P(A′)?

questp2-venn-regions#46.en: A and A′ together fill the whole sample space.

questp2-venn-regions#47.en: P(A) + P(A′) = 1 — together they cover everything.

questp2-venn-regions#52.en: One card of the word ${word} is drawn at random. Using the diagram, write P(vowel) as a fraction in simplest form.

questp2-venn-regions#53.en: Count the vowels inside the circle over the total number of letters.

questp3-venn-prob#5.en:
Roll a fair ${sc.N}-sided die. A = "${sc.descA}" = {${sc.A.join("; ")}}, B = "${sc.descB}" = {${sc.B.join("; ")}}.
How many outcomes are in A ∩ B?

questp3-venn-prob#6.en: A ∩ B = the values that appear in BOTH lists.

questp3-venn-prob#9.en:
Roll a fair ${sc.N}-sided die. A = "${sc.descA}" = {${sc.A.join("; ")}}, B = "${sc.descB}" = {${sc.B.join("; ")}}.
How many outcomes are in A but not B (only A)?

questp3-venn-prob#10.en: Take A and remove anything that is also in B.

questp3-venn-prob#13.en: Use the Venn diagram. Write P(A) as a fraction in simplest form.

questp3-venn-prob#14.en: P(A) = (only A + overlap) ÷ n(S). Don't forget the overlap!

questp3-venn-prob#17.en: Use the Venn diagram. Write P(A ∩ B) as a fraction in simplest form.

questp3-venn-prob#18.en: P(A ∩ B) = the overlap count ÷ n(S).

questp3-venn-prob#20.en: Use the Venn diagram. Write P(A ∪ B) as a fraction in simplest form.

questp3-venn-prob#21.en: P(A ∪ B) = only A + overlap + only B, all ÷ n(S).

questp3-venn-prob#27.en: Use the Venn diagram. Write P(${lbl}) (not ${useA ? "A" : "B"}) as a fraction in simplest form.

questp3-venn-prob#28.en: P(${lbl}) = everything that is NOT in ${useA ? "A" : "B"}, ÷ n(S). Or use 1 − P(${useA ? "A" : "B"}).

questp3-venn-prob#30.en: Use the Venn diagram. Write P((A ∪ B)′) — in neither A nor B — as a fraction in simplest form.

questp3-venn-prob#31.en: “Neither” is the count OUTSIDE both circles ÷ n(S).

questp3-venn-prob#33.en: Use the Venn diagram. Write P(only B) — in B but not A — as a fraction in simplest form.

questp3-venn-prob#34.en: Take the part of B that is OUTSIDE the overlap ÷ n(S).

questp4-rules#1.en: Given P(A) = ${dec(s.pA)}, P(B) = ${dec(s.pB)} and P(A ∩ B) = ${dec(s.pAB)}, find P(A ∪ B).

questp4-rules#2.en: P(A ∪ B) = P(A) + P(B) − P(A ∩ B). Subtract the overlap once.

questp4-rules#3.en: P(A ∪ B) = P(A) + P(B) − P(A ∩ B)

questp4-rules#4.en: Given P(A) = ${dec(s.pA)}, P(B) = ${dec(s.pB)} and P(A ∪ B) = ${dec(s.pUnion)}, find P(A ∩ B).

questp4-rules#5.en: Rearrange the addition rule: P(A ∩ B) = P(A) + P(B) − P(A ∪ B).

questp4-rules#6.en: P(A ∩ B) = P(A) + P(B) − P(A ∪ B)

questp4-rules#7.en: Event B is the complement of A. If P(A) = ${dec(s.pA)}, find P(B).

questp4-rules#10.en: A and B are mutually exclusive. If P(A) = ${dec(s.pA)} and P(B) = ${dec(s.pB)}, find P(A ∪ B).

questp4-rules#11.en: Mutually exclusive → P(A ∩ B) = 0, so P(A ∪ B) = P(A) + P(B).

questp4-rules#12.en: No overlap → P(A ∪ B) = P(A) + P(B) = ${dec(s.pA)} + ${dec(s.pB)} = ${dec(s.pUnion, 2)}

questp4-rules#13.en: Two events have P(A ∩ B) = ${dec(s.pAB)}. Are they mutually exclusive or mutually inclusive?

questp4-rules#19.en: Overlap of 0 → exclusive (can't happen together). Overlap ≠ 0 → inclusive.

questp4-rules#22.en: The Venn diagram shows the counts in each region. Are A and B mutually exclusive?

questp4-rules#23.en: Mutually exclusive means the overlap (A ∩ B) is empty — a 0 in the middle.

questp4-rules#24.en: The overlap is 0, so yes — mutually exclusive.

questp4-rules#25.en: The overlap is not 0, so no — they can happen together.

questp4-rules#26.en: n(A ∩ B) = 0 → A and B cannot happen together → mutually exclusive.

questp4-rules#27.en: n(A ∩ B) = ${inter} ≠ 0 → A and B can happen together → NOT mutually exclusive.

questp4-rules#29.en: together they cover the whole sample space (nothing is left outside)

questp4-rules#32.en: they have exactly the same outcomes

questp4-rules#33.en: “Exhaustive” = nothing left over outside the events.

questp4-rules#34.en: Exhaustive events leave no outcome outside — together they fill S.

questp4-rules#35.en: Which is the correct addition rule for any two events?

questp4-rules#36.en: P(A ∪ B) = P(A) + P(B) + P(A ∩ B)

questp4-rules#39.en: You must remove the overlap once so it isn't counted twice.

questp4-rules#40.en: P(A ∪ B) = P(A) + P(B) − P(A ∩ B). The last option only works when there's no overlap.

questp5-independence#26.en: What is the test for whether two events A and B are independent?

questp5-independence#27.en: check whether P(A ∩ B) = P(A) × P(B)

questp5-independence#30.en: check whether P(A ∪ B) = P(A) × P(B)

questp5-independence#33.en: A and B are independent with P(A) = ${dec(pA)} and P(B) = ${dec(pB)}. Find P(A ∩ B).

questp5-independence#34.en: Independent → multiply: P(A ∩ B) = P(A) × P(B).

questp5-independence#36.en: P(A) = ${dec(pA)}, P(B) = ${dec(pB)} and P(A ∩ B) = ${dec(pAB)}. Are A and B independent?

questp5-independence#37.en: Work out P(A) × P(B) = ${dec(prod, 2)} and compare it with P(A ∩ B).

questp5-independence#38.en: P(A) × P(B) = ${dec(prod, 2)}; P(A ∩ B) = ${dec(pAB)} → ${Math.abs(pAB - prod) < 1e-9 ? "equal, so independent" : "not equal, so NOT independent"}.

questp5-independence#40.en: Compare with P(A ∩ B) = ${dec(pAB)} → ${Math.abs(pAB - prod) < 1e-9 ? "independent" : "not independent"}.

questp5-independence#41.en: ${tableHTML(t)}One person is chosen at random. Write P(${x.rL}) as a fraction in simplest form.

questp5-independence#42.en: P(${x.rL}) = that row's total ÷ the grand total.

questp5-independence#43.en: ${tableHTML(t)}Write P(${x.rL} and ${x.cL}) as a fraction in simplest form.

questp5-independence#44.en: Use the single overlap cell ÷ the grand total.

questp5-independence#47.en: P(${x.rSym})×P(${x.cSym}) = ${dec(t.prodInter, 4).replace(/0+$/, "")} and P(${x.rSym} ∩ ${x.cSym}) = ${dec(t.realInter, 4).replace(/0+$/, "")} → ${t.independent ? "equal, so independent" : "not equal, so NOT independent"}.

questp5-independence#52.en: If P(A ∩ B) is not equal to P(A) × P(B), what can you say?

questp5-independence#53.en: A and B are not independent

questp5-independence#54.en: A and B are mutually exclusive

questp5-independence#57.en: The product rule only holds when events are independent.

questp5-independence#58.en: Product rule fails → the events are not independent.

questp6-trees#1.en: On a tree diagram, the probabilities on the branches leaving any single point must add up to…

questp6-trees#3.en: Those branches cover every option from that point.

questp6-trees#4.en: Branches from one point are exhaustive → they add up to 1.

questp6-trees#9.en: A biased coin has P(H) = ${dec(pH)}. Using the tree, find P(${path[0]}, ${path[1]}) — the path ${path}.

questp6-trees#10.en: Multiply the two branch probabilities ALONG the path.

questp6-trees#12.en: Two tosses of a coin. Tap the path that gives the outcome ${target[0][0]} then ${target[0][1]} (${target[0]}).

questp6-trees#13.en: Follow the first letter on the first set of branches, then the second.

questp6-trees#14.en: Read the outcome labels on the right: ${target[0]}.

questp6-trees#16.en: A coin with P(H) = ${dec(pH)} is tossed twice. Using the tree, find P(exactly one head).

questp6-trees#17.en: Which paths give exactly one head?

questp6-trees#22.en: Exactly one head means one H and one T — either order counts.

questp6-trees#24.en: Multiply ALONG the path: P(H) × P(T).

questp6-trees#26.en: Multiply ALONG the path: P(T) × P(H).

questp6-trees#27.en: Now P(exactly one head) — add the two paths.

questp6-trees#29.en: Exactly one head = the HT path OR the TH path. Multiply along each path, then ADD the two paths.

questp6-trees#34.en: A fair coin is tossed twice. Using the tree, find P(at least one head).

questp6-trees#35.en: Add the three paths with a head, or do 1 − P(no heads).

questp6-trees#37.en: P(at least one H) = P(HH) + P(HT) + P(TH) = 0,25 + 0,25 + 0,25 = 0,75

questp6-trees#39.en: What is the quickest way to work out P(at least one)?

questp6-trees#44.en: The opposite of “at least one” is “none at all”.

questp6-trees#46.en: A coin with P(H) = ${dec(pH)} is tossed twice. Find P(no heads).

questp6-trees#47.en: No heads = tails then tails: multiply the two tail branches.

questp6-trees#48.en: P(no H) = P(T) × P(T) = ${dec(1 - pH)} × ${dec(1 - pH)} = ${dec(v, 2)}

questp6-trees#49.en: Two identical biased coins are tossed. It is found that P(both heads) = ${dec(pHH)}. Find P(both tails).

questp6-trees#51.en: The coins are identical, so P(H) × P(H) = ${dec(pHH)} — take the square root to find P(H) first.

questp7-replacement#1.en: A bag holds ${N} balls. One is drawn and not replaced. How many balls are there for the second draw?

questp7-replacement#2.en: Without replacement, the ball is kept out — the total drops by one.

questp7-replacement#3.en: Without replacement the total falls from ${N} to ${N - 1}.

questp7-replacement#4.en: A bag has ${env.b.counts[c.k]} ${c.name} balls. One ${c.name} ball is drawn and not replaced. How many ${c.name} balls remain for the next draw?

questp7-replacement#5.en: The colour you took also drops by one.

questp7-replacement#6.en: Two balls are drawn from ${N}, ${replace ? "with" : "without"} replacement. Does the denominator change between the first and second draw?

questp7-replacement#7.en: With replacement, the ball goes back — nothing changes.

questp7-replacement#8.en: Without replacement, one ball is gone — the total changes.

questp7-replacement#9.en: With replacement the total stays ${N}, so the denominator does NOT change.

questp7-replacement#10.en: Without replacement it drops from ${N} to ${N - 1}, so the denominator DOES change.

questp7-replacement#11.en: A bag holds ${env.b.counts[env.cols[0].k]} ${env.cols[0].name} and ${env.b.counts[env.cols[1].k]} ${env.cols[1].name} balls. Two are drawn with replacement. Using the tree, find P(${p.k1}, ${p.k2}) in simplest form.

questp7-replacement#12.en: With replacement, both draws use the same total. Multiply along the path.

questp7-replacement#13.en: A bag holds ${env.b.counts[env.cols[0].k]} ${env.cols[0].name} and ${env.b.counts[env.cols[1].k]} ${env.cols[1].name} balls. Two are drawn without replacement. Using the tree, find P(${p.k1}, ${p.k2}) in simplest form.

questp7-replacement#14.en: Without replacement, the second denominator is one smaller — and the first colour drops by one.

questp7-replacement#15.en: A bag holds ${env.b.counts[env.cols[0].k]} ${env.cols[0].name} and ${env.b.counts[env.cols[1].k]} ${env.cols[1].name} balls. Two are drawn ${replace ? "with" : "without"} replacement. Find P(at least one ${c.name}) in simplest form.

questp7-replacement#20.en: Two balls drawn without replacement. Tap the path for ${env.name(p.k1)} then ${env.name(p.k2)} (${p.path}).

questp7-replacement#21.en: Match the outcome label on the right.
